task.description:
Measured in the cross-fixture yield study (.gaugeblock/storypole/plans/JN-9.md): 9 fills across 3 fixtures gave 3 Gold and 6 Silver, and the split is per-hole rather than per-pipeline. sum_positive is a one-line delegation that compiles first try, so it produced 0/3 Gold; parse_port needs range and error handling the first attempt plausibly gets wrong, so it produced 2/3. grapheme_count sat at 1/3.

CONSEQUENCE: running more fills over trivial holes yields more Silver and no DPO pairs. Growing the Gold corpus needs holes with genuine failure modes - wrong return types, error mapping, borrow lifetimes, trait bounds - not more fixtures of the same difficulty.

NEXT: build a fixture set graded by difficulty (a trivial delegation, an error-mapping case, a lifetime/borrow case, a trait-bound case) and measure Gold rate per grade. That would turn the 33% headline into a per-difficulty curve, which is what would tell us whether the corpus can be grown on purpose or only harvested opportunistically. Related: JN-9 (compiler oracle), GB-225 (body carrying), GB-228 (spool quarantine).
task.title: A trivial hole cannot produce a Gold pair, so the corpus cannot grow by repetition alone

events.description:
PARKED by owner decision 2026-10-30. Deliberately not pursued now: the pipeline defects that produced no Gold are all cleared (GB-224, GB-225, GB-227), and the owner is comfortable with Gold accruing organically rather than by manufacturing difficulty.

OWNER THESIS, worth preserving because it changes the ticket premise: Gold is inherently rarer here because the oracle and the universal provider are the same model right now - the verifier cannot be harder than the generator. The intended sources of Gold are instead (a) backfill and OSS mining over real messy git history - commits named fix, fix again, another try carry a genuine failed state and a genuine repair, which is exactly a DPO pair, and (b) community contributions once the public rabbet datastore exists and developers report their own traces.

So the grading idea below is not rejected, only deprioritised. Re-open if the corpus needs to be grown faster than real history supplies.
